what_changed.scope: _identifiers only - a pure function of file content
what_changed.lines_of_substance: a stat, a dict lookup, and a frozenset store
what_changed.nothing_else_touched: no gate decision, no blocker logic, no threshold, no strategy code, no params

why_each_part.resolved_path: two modules must not share an entry
why_each_part.st_mtime_ns: the ordinary change signal; NANOseconds because a coarse clock lets two edits inside one second look identical
why_each_part.st_size: the backstop mtime cannot provide - a same-second, same-timestamp rewrite. Getting past both needs two files of identical length AND an identical nanosecond timestamp

cache_key.why_frozen: the cached object is handed to every later caller; a mutable set would let one caller quietly edit what the next one measures
cache_key.what_is_NOT_cached: every gate decision, blocker list and measurement result - those read state no file timestamp can speak for

fail_closed_preserved.how: stat() runs BEFORE the cache is consulted, so a missing or unreadable file raises exactly as the read used to and is never answered from a remembered scan
fail_closed_preserved.the_distinction_being_protected: 'I cannot see the file' and 'I saw the file and it was clean' are the two answers this gate exists to keep apart
proven_by: a missing file raises and leaves NO cache entry
a file cached and then deleted raises on the next call

identifiers_calls_per_blocking_call.note: still called; now all cache hits

endpoint_cold_first_call.note: cold is dominated by the Stage 5ZZZ-S background warm-up workers saturating the CPU, not by the gate

proof_gate_output_unchanged.method: the FULL ledger - 11 blockers with every measured_now and required_measurement_now - captured before the edit and after, then compared as sorted JSON

mutations: key omits mtime -> caught by a SAME-SIZE edit
key omits size -> caught by a SAME-MTIME edit (timestamp forced back)
unreadable file treated as empty identifiers (fail-OPEN)
a cached file that disappears still served from cache
a blocker list stored in the cache instead of identifiers
tests.adversarial_note: the two invalidation tests use a same-SIZE edit and a same-MTIME edit on purpose. Either key part alone passes a naive test and misses a real change

regression.proven_how: every one was re-run with an UNCACHED `_identifiers` - the pre-stage logic byte for byte - and fails there too. Four ran standalone, the other three under a pytest plugin because they need fixtures
regression.what_they_actually_pin: a suite written 2026-08-22 that asserts track1_go_live_confirmation.json does NOT exist (the operator signed it 2026-08-27), a slot count of 70 against today's 71, and a ledger/registry comparison

tests.a_test_failed_first_run_for_a_real_reaso: the same-size test compared against len() of a Python string while Windows writes CRLF, so the on-disk sizes were 14 and my assertion said 13. It now compares the two on-disk sizes

backend_restart.why: to measure the endpoint against the new module

the_scheduler_still_runs_the_old_code.fact: the scheduler was NOT restarted, so pid 34564 still holds the pre-memoisation `track1_gates` in memory
the_scheduler_still_runs_the_old_code.consequence: the speed-up is live for the dashboard and for any newly started process; the scheduler picks it up whenever it is next restarted
the_scheduler_still_runs_the_old_code.is_this_a_problem: no - the change is performance-only and the gate output is byte-identical either way, so the two processes cannot disagree about whether orders are possible

answers.invalidation_proven: same-size edit caught by mtime, same-mtime edit caught by size, deleted file raises rather than serving a stale hit
answers.backend_restart: needed and done once; scheduler untouched
